title: Japan at the World Cup
description: The Blue Samurai have gone from World Cup newcomers to giant-killers — how well do you know Japan's journey?

questions.q: Japan made their World Cup debut in which year?
questions.explain: Japan qualified for their first World Cup at France 1998. They were eliminated in the group stage, but it was the beginning of a remarkable run of consecutive qualifications.

questions.q: Japan co-hosted the 2002 World Cup with which country?
questions.explain: Japan and South Korea co-hosted the 2002 World Cup — the first held in Asia and the first with two host nations. Japan reached the round of 16, where they were beaten 1–0 by Turkey.

questions.q: At the 2022 World Cup, Japan pulled off one of the tournament's biggest shocks by beating Germany. What was the final score?
questions.explain: Japan came from 1–0 down to beat Germany 2–1, with goals from Ritsu Doan and Takuma Asano in the second half. It was one of the great World Cup upsets.

questions.q: Japan also beat Spain in the 2022 group stage, sending the reigning European champions into crisis. What was the score?
questions.explain: Japan beat Spain 2–1, topping Group E ahead of Germany. They became only the second Asian side to top a World Cup group containing European nations.

questions.q: How did Japan's 2022 World Cup end, after topping their group?
options: Round of 16 loss to Croatia on penalties
questions.explain: Japan drew 1–1 with Croatia after extra time, then lost 3–1 on penalties. It was a heartbreaking end after such a memorable group stage.

questions.q: Which Japanese player is regarded as the greatest of his generation and played in Serie A for Perugia, Roma and Bologna?
questions.explain: Hidetoshi Nakata was the first Japanese player to make a major impact in Serie A, winning the UEFA Cup with Parma in 1999. He retired at 29 to pursue other interests — a decision that shocked the football world.

questions.q: Japan's national team is nicknamed the Blue Samurai. What colour are their home shirts?
questions.explain: Japan wear blue home shirts — hence the Samurai Blue nickname. The shade is inspired by the indigo blue traditionally associated with Japan.

questions.q: The 2002 World Cup final was held in Japan. Which city hosted it?
questions.explain: The 2002 World Cup final between Brazil and Germany (Brazil won 2–0) was held at the International Stadium Yokohama, capacity 72,000.

questions.q: Japan topped their group at the 2002 World Cup as co-hosts but were knocked out in the round of 16 by which team?
questions.explain: Turkey beat Japan 1–0 in the round of 16, ending the co-hosts' tournament. Japan had beaten Russia 1–0 in the group stage to top their group — the furthest they had gone at that point.

questions.q: Which Japanese player scored iconic goals in both the 2010 and 2014 World Cups, including against Cameroon and Ivory Coast?
questions.explain: Keisuke Honda scored in both the 2010 and 2014 World Cups, netting against Cameroon in 2010 and being one of Japan's most influential players across three tournaments.
